Vivify

VIV-uh-fy · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To vivify to bring to life, animate, or make more vivid and lively.

The elderly historian's hands trembled as he described how a single wartime letter could vivify decades-old memories he thought he'd forgotten.

Worked Example

A single well-chosen detail -- the smell of her grandmother's kitchen -- was enough to vivify an otherwise ordinary childhood memory.

To vivify something is to make it feel vividly alive in the mind, not just to describe it.

How Vivify Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

animate

animate: to give life or energy to something

energize

energize: to give vigor, spirit, or excitement to

Antonyms

deaden

deaden: to make dull, lifeless, or numb

dull

dull: to make less vivid, sharp, or lively

How Strong Is It? — brighten → electrify → vivify

brighten vs. vivify

brighten vs. vivify: Brighten means to make something a little more lively or cheerful, a milder change than vivify.

electrify vs. vivify

electrify vs. vivify: Electrify means to excite someone intensely, an even more powerful jolt of energy than simply vivifying something.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — viv-

root — viv-: alive, life (Latin vivus, 'alive')

suffix — -ify

suffix — -ify: to make (Latin -ficare)

Put it together

Put it together: Vivify comes from Latin vivus ('alive') + -ify ('to make') -- literally 'to make alive.'

Use the root in a new word: vivid

Use the root in a new word: vivid: Her vivid description of the shipwreck made the whole class feel like they were standing on the deck.

Word Choice

Vivify is a formal, almost literary word -- you'll see it more in writing about art, memory, or storytelling than in everyday conversation.
